items.title: Doug Carn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2023
items.q: A couple of years ago someone wrote a nice article about you, a fellow named Aaron Cohen

ctx.x: And so but they don’t get paid for that. You know? See actually I’m not being bitter or have an attitude about it, but record companies owe the jazz musicians half of all the money they made, the publishing companies too you know. Because they copyrighted and collected money through performance rights organizations of music that they did not create you know. If they was only going to get paid for owning the melody then you don’t need other stars to play you know? Just get a drum machine to keep the beat and let…

A couple of years ago someone wrote a nice article about you, a fellow named Aaron Cohen, “Doug Carn’s Big Moment.” And there’s a quote from you in it. It said, “My plan is you better get out of the way because I’m tired of holding back.” And I wonder if at various times in your career did you feel that you were held back from what you really wanted to do?

Yeah. I feel like that right now, because they got it as entertainment only. You know? Because if you look at that, those trees that they have with the roots of jazz you know, down at the bottom they got Satchmo and Bix Beiderbecke, and then they got, you know, the different people you know. And they come on up with Barney Bigard and —
